name: The Chark household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: chark_john_a

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 July 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-07-09, 8 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-07-16 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.name: John A. Chark

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'John A. Chark' and 'ohn A. Chark' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 5, reprinted over 2 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-09 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Chark' is one letter from Clark, h for l, and the forename 'John A.' agrees letter for letter with John A. Clark, in the Democrat of 11 February 1834 (#c001) — the same middle initial A. The stem 'Chark' is set nowhere in the deposited corpus and the town holds no other bearer of it: on the face of it a card minted off a garble.
merge_ruling.against_merge: A GARBLED READING CANNOT BE TESTED, AND THERE ARE TWO CLARKS IT COULD BE. R5 is the standing refusal and T-0695 is the ticket that reads these cards at the image; T-1027 files `chark_john_a` under the garbles in its own words — 'a fold here would repair a wreck by guessing at it'. The guess is not even single-valued: the town holds clark_john_a and clark_john_k, and the `clark-john` cluster has already ruled those two DISTINCT under D1 on their contradicting middle initials, so a fold of 'John A. Chark' would have to choose which of two ruled-apart men to join. Clark is set 2,655 times in the corpus and the reading index holds 37 Clark identities. R5, and the reading belongs to T-0695.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
